nodes.label: Deterministic Session Startup Sequence
nodes.rationale: A fixed read-order of core files at every session start guarantees memory continuity and prevents context loss between agent sessions; success indicator is 'no context loss between sessions'.

nodes.label: Memory System (long-term index + daily logs)
nodes.rationale: Split memory into a curated long-term index (MEMORY.md), append-only daily logs (memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md), and ground-truth data (data/*.yaml) so session memory survives agent context resets; append-never-overwrite preserves traceability via source_refs.

nodes.label: Subagent Delegation Patterns (swarm, pipeline, parallel research)
nodes.rationale: Cost-tiered model selection (Kimi-2.5/Big-Pickle for cheap extraction, Claude-Sonnet for quality review, GPT-4 for high-stakes approval) makes multi-agent work cost-effective; patterns are data swarms, three-tier review pipelines, and parallel research.
nodes.norm_label: subagent delegation patterns (swarm, pipeline, parallel research)

nodes.label: Autopoietic Agent Coordination (six principles)
nodes.rationale: The agent ecosystem is designed as a living emergent system rather than a rigid hierarchy: alignment without control, emergence over planning, self-organization, healthy role overlap, and conflict treated as design signal — because bottom-up patterns propagate better than top-down prescriptions.

nodes.label: Safety Policy (autonomous vs approval boundaries)
nodes.rationale: External communication, on-chain transactions, publishing, identity-file edits, and financial actions require operator approval; internal memory/schema work is autonomous. Design intent: 'When in doubt: draft and present, don't execute.' A two-tier operator/council pattern adds a second approval layer for major decisions.

nodes.label: Regen Agency Knowledge Commons
nodes.rationale: org-os acts as upstream reference: template changes flow downstream to forks, working patterns from nodes are extracted back into standards, and nodes sync versions monthly.

nodes.label: Agent Dojo (distributed agent learning network)
nodes.rationale: Knowledge is structured for both human and agent consumption with semantic (not hierarchical) routing, so agents are first-class participants who learn continuously from operational experience; org-os defines the structural patterns, sync protocols, and semantic standards.

nodes.label: Phase 1: Guided Interview (bootstrap-interviewer)
nodes.rationale: An interactive interview generates SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md, data/*.yaml, and federation.yaml automatically, working via CLI or web form so non-technical operators can bootstrap without editing files.

nodes.label: Phase 3: Ongoing Learning (continuous improvement)
nodes.rationale: After setup, the workspace enters a continuous loop: meeting processing builds operational memory, heartbeat monitoring surfaces blocked tasks, and the workspace-improver skill runs an autonomous autoresearch improvement cycle.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md — Claude Code Instructions for org-os
nodes.norm_label: claude.md — claude code instructions for org-os

nodes.label: IDENTITY.md — Organizational Identity
nodes.rationale: Bridges OpenClaw agent identity with EIP-4824 organizational identity (daoURI, chain, treasury, governance infra) so agents ground who they operate as at session startup.

nodes.label: EIP-4824 (DAO/organization identity standard)
nodes.rationale: EIP-4824/DAOstar (daoURI, membersURI, proposalsURI, etc.) is adopted as the interoperability backbone so every org instance publishes machine-readable identity via .well-known/ schemas generated from data/*.yaml.

nodes.label: Framework/Instance Feedback Loop
nodes.rationale: org-os forks into instances (refi-dao-os, refi-bcn-os, regen-coordination-os) which feed operational patterns back into the framework; a Pattern is defined as a solution that works across multiple instances — theory serves practice, not the reverse.

nodes.label: Framework Development Flow (analyze→design→test→document→sync→validate→commit)
nodes.rationale: Changes are tested in safe branches before syncing to instances via sync:upstream so live deployments never break; breaking changes require documented rationale and migration path.

nodes.label: Framework Agent Boundaries (autonomous vs approval)
nodes.rationale: Analysis, docs, skills, and branch testing are autonomous; merging to main template, dependency changes, breaking schema changes, and anything affecting deployed instances require approval — protecting downstream instances from framework churn.

nodes.label: Paperclip Agents App (Vue 3 dashboard + API/WebSocket server)
nodes.rationale: A non-technical dashboard (8 pages, 55+ endpoints) over org-os files: SQLite by default for zero-setup single users, PostgreSQL opt-in for teams; org-os files are never deleted, only updated, and git revert provides rollback.
nodes.norm_label: paperclip agents app (vue 3 dashboard + api/websocket server)

nodes.label: Paperclip Real-Time File Sync (watcher + WebSocket)
nodes.rationale: A file watcher with 300ms debounce plus WebSocket push means dashboard and org-os markdown/YAML files stay bidirectionally consistent with no manual sync and no server restarts — chosen so non-technical users never touch the CLI.

nodes.label: Cost-Tiered Model Allocation for Research
nodes.rationale: Cheap models (Kimi-2.5, Big-Pickle) handle ~80% of continuous discovery/scanning while top-tier models (Claude-Sonnet, GPT-4) do the ~20% of quarterly synthesis and strategy — establishing a research pipeline that improves org-os without bottlenecking human time.

nodes.label: Radicle (decentralized code collaboration)
nodes.rationale: Researched because org-os needs an abstraction layer above GitHub; Radicle + Egregore could potentially replace GitHub as the code substrate.

nodes.label: Gitcoin (grants + coordination)
nodes.rationale: The org-os website/hub design is inspired by Gitcoin's organizational visibility model and public knowledge commons.

nodes.label: Egregore (shared cognition / AI memory layer)
nodes.rationale: Described as 'our foundation' for team memory; Curve Labs (its builder) is tracked for deeper expertise and partnership on org-os integration.

nodes.label: Core Values (regenerative over extractive, local autonomy, open by default)
nodes.rationale: Values ground agent decisions: each node governs itself while sharing infrastructure not control; boundaries prohibit compromising member privacy, growth via ecological harm, and committing funds without community consent.
nodes.norm_label: core values (regenerative over extractive, local autonomy, open by default)

nodes.label: npm run sync (git-free interactive sync)
nodes.rationale: Simplifies git into four operations (pull/status/commit/push) behind an interactive menu so non-technical operators can sync without knowing git.

nodes.label: TOOLS.md — Local Tool Notes
nodes.rationale: Skills are shared across deployments while node-specific setup lives here; keeping them apart lets skills update without losing local notes and share without leaking infrastructure. Credentials are never stored, only referenced.

nodes.label: Semantic Versioning for Framework + Instances
nodes.rationale: SemVer 2.0.0 with instance build metadata (framework-version+instance-tag, e.g. 1.0.0+refi-bcn-2026-04-01) lets each deployed fork track both the upstream framework version and its local customizations independently.

nodes.label: dashboard.yaml — /initialize Dashboard Section Config
nodes.rationale: Sections can be toggled, reordered, and customized without deleting files, so each instance controls what /initialize shows (projects, tasks, calendar, funding, pipelines) declaratively.

nodes.label: federation.yaml — Federation Manifest v3.0
nodes.rationale: Single manifest declares identity (daoURI, chain, safe, hats, gardens), network peers with trust levels (full/read/none), upstream/downstream sync relationships, agent runtime + skills, knowledge-commons publishing policy, and cross-repo integrations.

nodes.label: /initialize Command — Open org-os Session
nodes.rationale: The dashboard is pre-rendered by scripts/initialize.mjs and output verbatim (no agent re-rendering) so formatting and section visibility are deterministic; a manual file-reading fallback covers missing dependencies.

nodes.label: Generate EIP-4824 Schemas GitHub Actions Workflow
nodes.rationale: Regenerates .well-known/ schemas on every push to data/, content, or federation.yaml plus a daily cron, committing as 'Org OS Bot' with [skip ci] — keeping published EIP-4824 identity in sync with source data without human action.
nodes.norm_label: generate eip-4824 schemas github actions workflow

nodes.label: Intake Agent
nodes.rationale: Maps to OpenClaw input-handler agent; funnels heterogeneous input into typed destinations so nothing lands unrouted.

nodes.label: Research Agent
nodes.rationale: Maps to OpenClaw knowledge-curator agent; grounds all synthesis in sources and dense WikiLinks — never invents content.

nodes.label: Reviewer Agent
nodes.rationale: Maps to OpenClaw project-reviewer agent; assesses portfolio via IDEA stage, activity recency, blockers, and temporal-note integration.

nodes.label: IDEA Framework (Integrate → Develop → Execute → Archive)
nodes.rationale: Shared project-lifecycle stage model used across agents so status, routing, and review speak the same vocabulary.

nodes.label: OPEN → PLAN → EXECUTE → CLOSE Session Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Design intent: the agent arrives already aware and oriented — a living system showing current state, not a blank slate. Every session should feel sharp, effortless, purposeful.
nodes.norm_label: open → plan → execute → close session lifecycle

nodes.label: Initialization Dashboard (Phase 1: OPEN)
nodes.rationale: Dashboard doubles as a launchpad ('Or:' line signals the operator can go anywhere); on malformed script output it degrades gracefully to direct file reads — never show an error to the operator.

nodes.label: Auto-Sync Session Bookends
nodes.rationale: Git pull before load, push after close, so the operator never has to remember syncing; on failure continue silently with local state — never block the session on a sync failure.

nodes.label: Session Close Protocol (Phase 4: CLOSE)
nodes.rationale: Commit + push is 'the whole point of close'; the memory write is never skipped because it is the thread that connects sessions.

nodes.label: Dashboard Visual Language (box-drawing, status glyphs)
nodes.rationale: Unicode box-drawing and block elements chosen because they render in all modern terminals and agent tools; factual only — no mission quotes or taglines.

nodes.label: Tech Tree Form A: Constellation (force-directed radial)
nodes.rationale: Organic 'egregore energy' with emergent layout; hybrid noted — constellation layout with status-driven radial gradient merges A's aliveness with B's frontier legibility.
nodes.norm_label: tech tree form a: constellation (force-directed radial)

nodes.label: Tech Tree Form B: Civ-style Tech Tree Columns
nodes.rationale: Deterministic left-to-right live → in-dev → planned → ideation columns; reads instantly as a roadmap ('the frontier is to the right'), trading organic feel for legibility.
nodes.norm_label: tech tree form b: civ-style tech tree columns

nodes.label: Tech Tree Form C: Living Tree (bottom-up organic)
nodes.rationale: Trunk/boughs/buds growth metaphor matching the autopoietic story; hierarchy primary, cross-cutting dependencies drawn faintly as secondary.
nodes.norm_label: tech tree form c: living tree (bottom-up organic)

nodes.label: Aesthetic A: Blueprint Schematic (light systems theme)
nodes.rationale: Ink nodes on warm paper over blueprint grid, consistent with every other site page; chosen as the light-theme half of the final Blueprint+Observatory pairing.
nodes.norm_label: aesthetic a: blueprint schematic (light systems theme)

nodes.label: Aesthetic B: Dark Observatory (star chart)
nodes.rationale: Full-bleed dark star-chart for maximum 'alive egregore' drama — a deliberate break from the paper pages; chosen as the dark-theme half of the final pairing.

nodes.label: Aesthetic C: Adaptive Token-Native Theming
nodes.rationale: Draws entirely from the site's theme token contract with no special-casing — cleanest architecture; the graph inherits any future theme for free, sleekness comes from motion and typography rather than glow.

nodes.label: Federation Map Scope A: External-Only Map
nodes.rationale: Clean separation — Obsidian graph is inside, this map is outside; simplest data model.
nodes.norm_label: federation map scope a: external-only map

nodes.label: Federation Map Scope B: Continuum with Boundary Notes
nodes.rationale: Includes KB objects with external provenance as an inner cluster so a note can be traced to its source and originating peer — one continuous inside → outside space.
nodes.norm_label: federation map scope b: continuum with boundary notes

nodes.label: Federation Map Scope C: Two Linked Views
nodes.rationale: CHOSEN (waiting-1: 'Scope locked: C'). Map stays strictly external but boundary nodes deep-link between internal graph and federation map — parallel views with wormholes/portals between them.
nodes.norm_label: federation map scope c: two linked views

nodes.label: Federation Map Style A: Orbital Observatory
nodes.rationale: Concentric rings by hop-distance, deterministic (same data → same map), evolves the existing FederationGraph.astro directly. Final decision (waiting-2): hybrid — orbital structure × constellation physics × torchlight atmosphere.
nodes.norm_label: federation map style a: orbital observatory

nodes.label: Federation Map Style B: Constellation (d3-force)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately rhymes with Obsidian's internal graph view so the two linked views feel like the same instrument pointed inward vs outward; contributes physics to the chosen hybrid.

nodes.label: Federation Map Style C: Torchlight
nodes.rationale: Light falls off with hop-distance, frontier nodes as faint embers; most atmospheric but slightly more work to keep legible/accessible — contributes atmosphere to the chosen hybrid.

nodes.label: Agent Modes Pattern
nodes.rationale: Modes augment, not replace, the core behavior in AGENTS.md. Mode = how the agent behaves (persona, priorities, communication style); skill = what the agent can do. Only one mode is active at a time; modes reference skills but skills never reference modes.

nodes.label: Agent File Set
nodes.rationale: Human-controlled files (SOUL, IDENTITY, MASTERPLAN) set direction; agent-controlled files (memory/, HEARTBEAT updates) track execution; MEMORY.md is shared — agents log, humans curate.

nodes.label: MASTERPLAN.md Agent Compass
nodes.rationale: Modeled on karpathy/autoresearch's program.md: the single most important human-authored file, the only sanctioned surface for steering autonomous agent behavior over time (activations, research directions, success metrics, boundaries).

nodes.label: Three-Tier Skills Architecture
nodes.rationale: Core skills come from the framework, custom skills are instance-specific, and proven custom skills are promoted upstream (instance proposes via PR, framework generalizes, other instances inherit via sync:upstream).

nodes.label: Agent Safety Policy
nodes.rationale: Autonomous actions (read, memory logs, schema generation, drafting) require no approval; external messages, on-chain transactions, publishing, and identity-file changes require human approval. When uncertain, default to draft-and-present.

nodes.label: Knowledge Commons Layer
nodes.rationale: Knowledge Commons is the CENTER of the architecture — decisions are captured/stored/distributed, patterns extracted/curated/shared, agent learnings reflected/aggregated/trained; cross-instance sync is knowledge-first.

nodes.label: Autoresearch Pattern
nodes.rationale: One change per cycle so each improvement is independently evaluable and reversible; measure baseline first; agents modify only a scoped editable surface (mirroring autoresearch's train.py constraint); MASTERPLAN.md is the only way humans change agent direction; conservative by default — when in doubt, flag for human review.

nodes.label: Scoped Editable Surface
nodes.rationale: data/*.yaml, knowledge/, memory/, skills/, ideas/, .well-known/, HEARTBEAT.md are agent-modifiable; SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md, federation.yaml, MASTERPLAN.md, package.json are human-controlled — mirrors autoresearch's rule that agents modify train.py but never prepare.py or program.md.

nodes.label: Chat Interface Contract
nodes.rationale: Read operations always available; write operations require confirmation; identity files, financial transactions, governance structure, and skill deployment are never modifiable via chat — those require CLI/GitHub.

nodes.label: Sync Command
nodes.rationale: Wraps git in npm run sync so operators without git knowledge can pull/status/commit/push safely via an interactive menu.

nodes.label: org-os Data Model (13 Registries)
nodes.rationale: All organizational data lives as YAML registries in data/ as the single source of truth — schemas, dashboards, and agent queries all read from them; after any change run generate:schemas and validate:schemas.

nodes.label: Federation Protocol
nodes.rationale: Federation is opt-in, additive, and sovereignty-preserving — it adds visibility, not control. Git is the substrate because every org-os instance is already a Git repo, enabling PR/submodule/direct-read exchange without new infrastructure; koi-net is optionally layered on top for real-time sync.

nodes.label: federation.yaml Manifest v3.0
nodes.rationale: Root configuration file from which all federation behavior derives; the customizations section is critical for upstream sync safety — without maintain_on_sync entries an upstream merge could overwrite organization-specific files.

nodes.label: Knowledge Exchange Protocol
nodes.rationale: The primary value of federation: share curated knowledge across boundaries while maintaining data sovereignty, via publish (knowledge-manifest + .well-known/knowledge.json) and subscribe (git, koi-net, or manual sync).

nodes.label: Hatched Repo Federation
nodes.rationale: Creates a virtuous cycle: the parent org generates ideas, the best ones hatch into project repos, and those projects feed knowledge back into the parent's commons via bidirectional subscription.

nodes.label: Knowledge-to-Projects Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Transforms an org from a passive knowledge holder into an active ecosystem developer: knowledge is processed into ideas, ideas are curated through a lifecycle, and approved ideas hatch into standalone federated project repos — the org takes agency in filling ecosystem gaps.

nodes.label: Compensation Models
nodes.rationale: Not built in v2 but the data model is future-ready: compensation.model in ideas.yaml tracks bounty/retroactive/grants/equity mechanisms, linking to funding-opportunities and finances registries; Gardens conviction voting could prioritize which ideas get funded.

nodes.label: Access Tiers
nodes.rationale: Four tiers (Public, Network, Core, Private) mitigate the risk of financial details, personal info, or pre-decision deliberations leaking into the shared commons; sensitive items get manual curation with designated reviewers.

nodes.label: Operator Access Levels
nodes.rationale: Five levels (L0 chat to L4 direct editing) let non-developers use org-os fully — start at Level 0 and move up only if desired; each level strictly widens capability without requiring the ones above it.

nodes.label: knowledge_base Package
nodes.rationale: Cannot be disabled — it is the foundation of org-os, providing the base directory structure, template files, EIP-4824 schema infrastructure, and Git-based versioning.

nodes.label: Autopoietic Agent Coordination
nodes.rationale: Living emergent system where agents share context but keep autonomy; alignment without control, emergence over planning, conflict treated as signal — parallel experiments beat forced consensus.

nodes.label: Nine-Step Deterministic Startup Sequence
nodes.rationale: Ordered outer layer to inner layer: values before operations (SOUL before HEARTBEAT), environmental awareness before action (TOOLS before execution), validation last to prevent stale schema deployments.

nodes.label: Subagent Delegation with Model Tiers
nodes.rationale: Cost-efficient task distribution: cheap models for file I/O and synthesis, mid-tier for quality review, expensive models reserved for final approval — significant cost savings without quality loss.

nodes.label: Workfront-Based Priority Tracking
nodes.rationale: Named workfronts with status, ownership, deliverables give clear accountability and surface blockers early; visible in all HEARTBEAT.md files.

nodes.label: Two-Tier Safety Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Safety holds when boundaries are clearly articulated: autonomous tier for workspace files and drafts, approval tier for external comms, on-chain actions, identity changes, and financial actions.

nodes.label: Success Metrics + Next Actions
nodes.rationale: Metrics give agents a north star; prioritized next actions at three timeframes (session/week/month) prevent decision paralysis.

nodes.label: Federation Through Shared Data
nodes.rationale: Nodes stay aligned by sharing context via federation.yaml, skills/, knowledge commons, and GitHub Actions automation — no centralized control, each node keeps autonomy.

nodes.label: Daily Memory + Auto-Commit
nodes.rationale: Append-only daily memory plus 30-minute auto-commit gives zero-effort continuity; git history serves as audit trail.

nodes.label: Organizational OS as Living System
nodes.rationale: The template should enable living systems, not enforce rigid structure — customization placeholders, patterns to adapt to local context, federation mechanisms for knowledge flow.

nodes.label: Plan Management Convention
nodes.rationale: Every instance uses docs/agent-plans/ with a QUEUE.md pipeline index and one plan per file with YAML frontmatter, enabling scoping, sequencing, and parallel execution across sessions; only 1-3 plans active at a time.

nodes.label: Plan Lifecycle (scoping to queued to active to completed)
nodes.norm_label: plan lifecycle (scoping to queued to active to completed)

nodes.label: Pull-Based Task Management
nodes.rationale: Agent picks tasks during natural breaks rather than interrupting the user unless P0 critical; all work visible, prioritized P0-P3, categorized, and time-bounded.

nodes.label: Egregore-Assisted Setup Path
nodes.rationale: AI-augmented coordination with persistent Git-based team memory — best for distributed async teams doing knowledge-intensive work with context handoffs.

nodes.label: Filesystem-Native Setup Path
nodes.rationale: Direct file editing with minimal abstraction, AI-optional — chosen for full control, minimal dependencies, and high-security contexts.

nodes.label: Hybrid Setup Path
nodes.rationale: Toggle between egregore and filesystem modes per session; same git repo and data files, so team members can each choose their preferred mode.

nodes.label: Three-Tier Skill Model (core/custom/shared)
nodes.rationale: Core skills ship with the framework, custom skills serve one instance's unique needs, and shared skills are custom skills promoted to the framework after proving value.

nodes.label: Skill Promotion Protocol (5-Step)
nodes.rationale: Create → prove value in 5+ sessions → propose to framework via PR or federation.yaml → framework review generalizes it → other instances inherit via sync:upstream.

nodes.label: Skill Discovery (trigger matching, explicit invocation, contextual activation)
nodes.norm_label: skill discovery (trigger matching, explicit invocation, contextual activation)

nodes.label: Notion-YAML Sync
nodes.rationale: Notion is the live source for day-to-day updates, YAML is the versioned ground truth; conflict resolution is timestamp-based with conflicts flagged in memory/ for review.

nodes.label: Subproject Matrix (5 layers x 5 repos)
nodes.rationale: Plan split as a matrix of feature layers (rows) x repos (columns) so each cell is independently executable, enabling parallel execution.

nodes.label: Autoresearch Pattern (Autonomous Workspace Improvement)
nodes.rationale: Maps karpathy/autoresearch onto org-os: MASTERPLAN.md = program.md, data/*.yaml + skills/ = train.py (editable surface), HEARTBEAT metrics = val_bpb, memory/ = experiment log. Agents improve the workspace within scoped boundaries (never SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md, federation.yaml) and log before/after metrics; humans steer via MASTERPLAN directions.

nodes.label: Idea Hatching Pipeline (Knowledge → Ideas → Hatched Projects)
nodes.rationale: org-os is a coordination layer for ecosystem development, not just internal ops: knowledge feeds surfaced ideas, approved ideas hatch into standalone repos scaffolded from the template that federate back to the parent org.
nodes.norm_label: idea hatching pipeline (knowledge → ideas → hatched projects)

nodes.label: Progressive Disclosure (Non-Tech Operator Accessibility)
nodes.rationale: Requiring GitHub+CLI excludes most community members; five levels (chat → web dashboard → guided bootstrap → CLI → direct repo editing) let operators do meaningful work at every level, with higher levels unlocking more power but never required for basics.

nodes.label: Repo Consolidation
nodes.rationale: Parallel standalone repos in 03 Libraries/ duplicate repos already cloned inside org-os instances, creating confusion about which is canonical; consolidate via repos.manifest.json then remove standalone duplicates.

nodes.label: MASTERPLAN.md
nodes.rationale: Standardized (replacing MASTERPROMPT.md) as the most important human-authored file — where operators write activations, research directions, success metrics, and boundaries to steer autonomous agent behavior over time.

nodes.label: Practical Knowledge Commons
nodes.rationale: Knowledge commoning: capture at the source while fresh, review before sharing (quality over quantity), link and connect; grows through consistent small practices, not heroic efforts.

nodes.label: Future Instance Specs Plan (regen-coordination-os and regen-toolkit)
nodes.norm_label: future instance specs plan (regen-coordination-os and regen-toolkit)

nodes.label: Egregore (Git-based AI Memory)
nodes.rationale: Shared intelligence layer for Claude Code teams: git-based persistent memory across sessions and people, async handoffs, no servers or accounts required — everything local via Git.

nodes.label: Knowledge Commons Three-Layer Architecture (Capture / Structure / Distribution)
nodes.rationale: Layer 1 AI-powered capture (OPAL, Egregore, KOI), Layer 2 human-reviewed structure in knowledge/, Layer 3 federation distribution (hub-node sync, skill distribution Mondays, knowledge aggregation Mondays, council Fridays).
nodes.norm_label: knowledge commons three-layer architecture (capture / structure / distribution)

nodes.label: knowledge/ Directory (domains, patterns, insights, entities, from-nodes)
nodes.norm_label: knowledge/ directory (domains, patterns, insights, entities, from-nodes)

nodes.label: Knowledge Sync Protocols (Hub→Nodes, Nodes→Hub, Peer Sync)
nodes.norm_label: knowledge sync protocols (hub→nodes, nodes→hub, peer sync)

nodes.label: KOI Network (Knowledge Organization Infrastructure)
nodes.rationale: Distributed protocol for federated knowledge graphs: network-wide sharing via RIDs, event-driven sync (NEW/UPDATE/FORGET), partial or full coordinator node types.

nodes.label: OPAL (AI-Powered Knowledge Garden)
nodes.rationale: Extracts entities (people, orgs, patterns, concepts) from documents with human-in-the-loop review before adding to the knowledge base; local-first with git persistence, 23 slash commands.

nodes.label: Human-in-the-Loop Review Workflow (_staging → review → knowledge/)
nodes.rationale: All AI extractions pass through a staging approval queue (approve/reject/edit) before entering the knowledge base — quality gate between AI capture and organizational memory.

nodes.label: OPAL (AI Knowledge Garden)
nodes.rationale: OPAL performs AI entity extraction (people, orgs, patterns) with confidence scoring locally, keeping heavy AI processing out of the bridge; it complements KOI, which handles network-wide federation.

nodes.label: OPAL Bridge
nodes.rationale: The bridge exists to translate between OPAL's AI-extracted entities and org-os structured YAML registries, deliberately routing all extractions through staging and human review before they become trusted storage. Total pipeline latency is bottlenecked by human review by design.

nodes.label: Human Review Queue
nodes.rationale: AI extraction accuracy is only 80-95% depending on entity type, so a confidence-based decision matrix gates auto-approval: high-confidence people/orgs may auto-approve, but decisions and action items always require explicit human review (3 reviewers) because they trigger organizational consequences. Trade-off accepted: review is the pipeline latency bottleneck (1-48 hrs) in exchange for trusted storage.

nodes.label: Solo Mode
nodes.rationale: Single-user mode: author approves own extractions and commits directly to main, chosen for individual operators and testing where PR overhead adds no value.

nodes.label: Commons Mode
nodes.rationale: Team mode: extractions flow through PR-based review with optional voting so shared knowledge requires collective approval before merge — governance over shared truth.

nodes.label: KOI (Distributed Knowledge Network)
nodes.rationale: KOI broadcast is optional and consent-based: local knowledge only leaves the org after human approval, keeping OPAL usable standalone without network sharing.

nodes.label: Research Quest Workflow
nodes.rationale: Quests exist to preserve research continuity across multiple sessions: findings accumulate under a quest ID and are exported to the knowledge base on close, rather than being lost between sessions.

nodes.label: Team Handoff Workflow
nodes.rationale: Handoffs capture pending reviews, active quests, recent decisions, and blockers so context survives operator switches, vacations, and session ends.

nodes.label: Federation Sync Workflow
nodes.rationale: Knowledge flows hub-to-nodes for skill distribution and nodes-to-hub for weekly knowledge aggregation, with peer sync (ReFi DAO ↔ ReFi BCN) bidirectional — separating distribution direction from aggregation direction.

nodes.label: Distributed Coordination
nodes.rationale: Holographic voting: decisions emerge from multiple small-group deliberations rather than large plenary sessions, a pattern observed in successful ReFi DAO gatherings.

nodes.label: Quadratic Voting
nodes.rationale: Chosen for community treasury allocation because it gives more voice to smaller contributors while preventing whale dominance.

nodes.label: Circular Funding Models
nodes.rationale: Returns from successful projects flow back into the funding pool to create a sustainable cycle, aligning with regenerative economics principles.

nodes.label: Organizational OS Knowledge Commons Index
nodes.rationale: org-os is deliberately a framework/template knowledge commons — reference material only. Knowledge aggregation is the hub's (Regen Coordination) role; org-os is upstream pattern source whose template changes propagate to all downstream forks.

nodes.label: Agent Dojo
nodes.rationale: Knowledge commons for AI agents learning to coordinate regenerative systems. Principles: agents are first-class participants, knowledge flows via semantic routing not hierarchy, local autonomy with global coherence, continuous learning from operational experience.

nodes.label: Memory Directory (Daily Logs)
nodes.rationale: Two-tier memory design: memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md holds detailed daily logs (kept 90 days) while MEMORY.md is the curated long-term index that references them — detail vs. summary separation.

nodes.label: Agents Application for ReFi Barcelona
nodes.rationale: Replaces the Telegram bot and CLI commands with a visual dashboard for managing agent tasks, monitoring costs, and coordinating cooperative formation work.

nodes.label: Agents App (@org-os/agents-app)
nodes.rationale: No database as source of truth — the org-os filesystem (federation.yaml, AGENTS.md, skills/) is the single source of truth, with Paperclip reading files and a React dashboard on top. Zero-config setup auto-detects an existing org.

nodes.label: Paperclip Runtime Configuration
nodes.rationale: Security section requires human approval for external messages, financial actions, agent hiring, and budget changes — the same draft-and-present safety posture as the wider org-os framework.

nodes.label: Agents App Implementation Checklist (P1/P2 Roadmap)
nodes.rationale: P0 shipped with embedded storage and mock data; PostgreSQL, real sync, and auth are deferred to P1, and Telegram is sunset only after feature parity and team comfort — an incremental migration strategy.

nodes.label: Egregore
nodes.rationale: Git-based shared intelligence layer chosen so Claude Code teams get persistent cross-session memory and async handoffs with no servers or accounts required — everything local via Git, works offline, no external SaaS dependency (lightweight alternative to Notion sync).

nodes.label: Egregore OpenCode Adapter
nodes.rationale: Egregore was originally designed for Claude Code's slash-command patterns; OpenCode lacks native /reflect, /handoff, /quest, so the adapter maps them onto OpenCode's /ask prefix convention ('Reflect:', 'Handoff:', 'Quest:') plus git commits — making AI memory portable across runtimes so mixed teams share one memory repo.

nodes.label: Egregore Command Mapping
nodes.rationale: Compatibility table translating each Egregore intent (reflect, handoff, quest, activity, save) into an OpenCode-equivalent invocation; quest IDs are kept portable across both runtimes as long as both users point at the same EGREGORE_MEMORY_REPO.

nodes.label: KOI Bridge
nodes.rationale: Standalone ~700-line TypeScript skeleton (bridge.ts, rid.ts, events.ts, git-sync.ts, cli.ts) connecting an org-os git repo to distributed KOI knowledge networks; status is skeleton-ready, needs a coordinator connection for full operation.

nodes.label: KOI-net Protocol
nodes.rationale: Distributed knowledge graph protocol from BlockScience/Metagov/RMIT; nodes federate git repos through a coordinator with a routing table.

nodes.label: KOI/OPAL Bridge
nodes.rationale: Integration layer connecting two complementary knowledge systems: OPAL (AI librarian, org-level gardens, human-in-the-loop) and KOI (protocol, network-scale RID-based graphs). Bridged because neither alone gives both local AI extraction quality and global federation reach.

nodes.label: OPAL (AI Librarian)
nodes.rationale: Organization-level AI-powered knowledge garden: /process extracts entities from meetings/documents, /review keeps a human in the loop, /ask answers questions; strength is AI extraction with human curation.

nodes.label: RID (Resource Identifier)
nodes.rationale: Typed identifiers (rid:orgos:person, rid:orgos:pattern, rid:orgos:meeting, ...) that map OPAL entities and org-os data registries onto the KOI network, enabling attribution and consent-based sharing.

nodes.label: Cosmo-Local Knowledge
nodes.rationale: Design intent of the KOI/OPAL integration: local AI-powered knowledge gardens that federate into global knowledge networks — knowledge is curated locally with human review but shared network-wide via RIDs.

nodes.label: CopyFair Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Both OPAL (git history + extraction provenance) and KOI (RID-based attribution, consent-based sharing) track attribution; together they enable CopyFair — contributions tracked, attribution preserved, value flows to contributors.

nodes.label: Agent Dojo
nodes.rationale: Agent training concept from Regen Agency: well-maintained knowledge gardens (via OPAL/KOI) train better agents; gardens are the foundation of the training pipeline.

nodes.label: Human-in-the-Loop Review
nodes.rationale: Quality gate in every workflow: OPAL-extracted entities must pass /review human approval before being broadcast as RIDs to the KOI network — entities not appearing in KOI is diagnosed first by checking whether /review approval happened.

nodes.label: OPAL Bridge CI/CD Workflow
nodes.rationale: GitHub Actions pipeline for packages/opal-bridge: build/lint/test with coverage, integration tests, OPAL integration tests against a synthetic OPAL instance (_inbox/_staging/_approved/_rejected/handoffs), npm release packaging, CodeQL security scan, and SSH-based deploys.

nodes.label: Hub-and-Nodes Federated Deployment
nodes.rationale: Deployment mirrors the federation topology: main-branch pushes deploy first to the hub (regen-coordination-os, with ENABLE_FEDERATION=true) and via a matrix to the nodes (refi-dao-os, refi-bcn-os), each with its own SSH credentials and production environment.

nodes.label: Meetings Package
nodes.rationale: Meeting management via markdown templates in content/meetings/; frontmatter plus inline action-item/decision formats are parsed by schema generation into an EIP-4824 compliant meetings.json in .well-known/.

nodes.label: Action Item Format
nodes.rationale: Structured inline syntax '- [ ] description (@assignee, due: YYYY-MM-DD) #action-id' chosen so action items and decisions stay human-readable in notes yet are automatically extractable into schemas and the task manager webapp; IDs auto-generate if missing.

nodes.label: ReFi BCN Retrospective Template
nodes.rationale: Beyond standard retro sections, includes alignment/data-quality checks: stakeholder map vs data/relationships.yaml, funding values vs knowledge/normalization-log.md canonical values, and source-of-truth link validity across upstream repositories.

nodes.label: IDEA Framework
nodes.rationale: Four-stage project lifecycle — Integrate (gather context/requirements), Develop (plan/roadmap/design), Execute (implement/deliver), Archive (reflect/evaluate/distill knowledge) — chosen so projects end with explicit knowledge capture rather than just completion; project status field maps 1:1 to stages.

nodes.label: IDEA Project Template
nodes.rationale: Archive stage includes a normalization-impact checklist (update knowledge/normalization-log.md canonical values, sync affected data/ registries) so project learnings propagate back into the org's source-of-truth data.

nodes.label: Paperclip Agents App
nodes.rationale: Paperclip as the agents application of org-os: zero-config recognition of federation.yaml, AGENTS.md, skills/, memory/, .well-known/org.json means any org-os instance gets a full agents dashboard (Fastify API on 3100, Vue 3 UI, PostgreSQL/SQLite) with just npm run setup — no CLI needed for non-technical users; multi-org support gives each instance an isolated Paperclip.

nodes.label: Paperclip SyncOrchestrator
nodes.rationale: Central sync coordinator (src/server/sync-orchestrator.ts) for bidirectional file <-> DB <-> UI sync: auto-sync on file changes, API-triggered pull/push, 100-event sync history buffer, conflict resolution.

nodes.label: Paperclip FileWatcher
nodes.rationale: Chokidar-based watcher (src/server/file-watcher.ts) monitoring org-os files (AGENTS.md, federation.yaml, skills/, memory/) with debounced change detection (300ms default) and automatic categorization.

nodes.label: Paperclip WebSocket Server
nodes.rationale: src/server/ws.ts: client management with 7 subscription types (org, agents, skills, tasks, memory, federation, sync), message routing/broadcast, keep-alive; paired with a Vue 3 useWebSocket composable with 3s auto-reconnection.

nodes.label: PARA Method
nodes.rationale: Projects, Areas, Resources, Archive — organizational scheme used by the memory routes and Memory page for daily notes, fact recording, timeline, tagging and cross-references.

nodes.label: OrgOsAdapter (bridge/org-os-adapter.ts)
nodes.rationale: 480+ line Phase 1 core: reads federation.yaml, AGENTS.md, skills/ to auto-discover org-os instances; built overnight 2026-03-29 using zen/big-pickle for architecture and zen/claude-haiku-4-5 for implementation.

nodes.label: Paperclip App Federation Config
nodes.rationale: Declares runtime behavior: 30m heartbeats, cost tracking with $200 default budget, multi-org mode, bidirectional org-os sync every 5m, egregore sync every 5m, and auto-discovery by walking up directories for federation.yaml / AGENTS.md / .well-known/org.json.

nodes.label: @org-os/org-os-bridge
nodes.rationale: Bridge package extracted for reuse: auto-discovery by directory-tree walking, federation.yaml parsing, AGENTS.md agent extraction, skills/ indexing, real-time file watching, and bidirectional sync with configurable conflict resolution (prefer-local | prefer-remote | manual).

nodes.label: Paperclip docker-compose
nodes.rationale: postgres:16-alpine with healthcheck-gated startup of the paperclip service on port 3100; mounts the parent directory as /app/org-os so the container sees the live org-os instance.

nodes.label: Regen Agents Package
nodes.rationale: Four specialist agents for regenerative organizations (DAOs, cooperatives, land stewardship groups), all following one directory pattern (index.ts, skills/, prompts/, examples/, AGENT.md) and all configured with model zen/kimi-k2.5; a Super Agent coordinates when a request needs multiple perspectives.

nodes.label: Super Agent
nodes.rationale: Coordinator that fans a complex request (e.g. 'design a regenerative land stewardship program') across multiple specialist agents and assembles deliverables like practice guide + governance framework + stakeholder map.

nodes.label: Commons Governance Specialist
nodes.rationale: DAO/cooperative governance analysis, legal wrapper comparison, dispute resolution design; tools governance-decision-tracker.ts and commons-governance.ts implement full Ostrom 8-principles assessment with risk identification.

nodes.label: Impact Measurement Analyst
nodes.rationale: IRIS+/GIIN standards-aligned metric design, trend/anomaly analysis, SDG alignment; tools impact-tracker.ts (seasonality detection, dashboards) and value-flow-tracker.ts (value chain mapping, multiplier calculation, equity analysis).

nodes.label: Bioregional Intelligence Agent
nodes.rationale: Watershed-based territory mapping, resource flow analysis (water/carbon/nutrients/energy), stakeholder power-dynamics mapping; tools bioregional-mapper.ts and local-node-connector.ts integrate sensor/community data with knowledge-sovereignty guidelines.

nodes.label: Regenerative Agriculture Researcher
nodes.rationale: Agent spec: model zen/kimi-k2.5, max 50 turns, tools Read/Write/Edit/WebSearch/WebFetch, skills research-orchestrator, pattern-recognition, knowledge-curator; four-step methodology (context analysis, evidence gathering, synthesis, practical translation) with quality standards requiring peer-reviewed citations, practitioner perspectives, and explicit confidence/uncertainty.

nodes.label: Agriculture Researcher System Prompt
nodes.rationale: Fixed output structure (executive summary, key findings with confidence ratings, practical implications, research gaps, next steps) plus citation rules (DOI when available, distinguish correlation from causation) and a tone that is rigorous yet accessible and respectful of farmer knowledge.

nodes.label: Evidence Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Five-level confidence ranking — meta-analyses/systematic reviews (highest), peer-reviewed field trials, on-farm research networks, case studies/farmer observations, expert opinion (lowest) — so every claim carries an honest confidence level and context-sensitivity (climate, soil, scale, market access, farmer capacity) is always weighed.

nodes.label: Bioregion
nodes.rationale: Defined by natural features (watersheds preferred, ecosystems, geology, cultural patterns, species distributions) rather than political borders, because political jurisdictions fragment ecological systems; scale tiers micro/meso/macro chosen to match watershed, basin, and biome analysis.

nodes.label: Ostrom's Eight Design Principles
nodes.rationale: Elinor Ostrom's empirically derived principles (boundaries, proportional equivalence, collective choice, monitoring, graduated sanctions, conflict resolution, recognition of rights, nested enterprises) are used as the evaluation rubric because they predict durable common-pool resource governance; the agent rates compliance principle-by-principle rather than applying generic best practices.

nodes.label: Theory of Change
nodes.source_location: Analysis Framework > Theory of Change Review
nodes.rationale: Causal chain (Inputs → Activities → Outputs → Outcomes → Impact) is reviewed first so claims distinguish outputs from outcomes and attribution from contribution, avoiding overclaiming impact (deadweight, displacement, drop-off).

nodes.label: Task Manager Webapp
nodes.rationale: Vanilla JavaScript with LocalStorage was chosen (no frameworks) to keep the webapp dependency-free and offline-capable; tasks are read from generated .well-known JSON rather than raw YAML so the UI consumes the same machine-readable surface as external consumers.

nodes.label: Federation Manifest v3.0 Specification
nodes.rationale: v3.0 extends v2.0 with agent configuration, skill declarations, and knowledge commons because federated org workspaces became agent-native; simple upstream/downstream links were replaced by network/hub/peers with explicit per-peer trust levels (full/read/none) to govern federation safely.

nodes.label: EIP-4824 Standard
nodes.rationale: EIP-4824 (daoURI JSON-LD) anchors organizational identity so any org node is machine-discoverable at /.well-known/dao.json, enabling on-chain registration and interoperable federation.

nodes.label: Knowledge Commons
nodes.rationale: Federated knowledge sharing uses declared shared-domains with explicit publish (meetings summaries, projects, funding) and subscribe rules so nodes contribute and receive knowledge selectively; summaries not transcripts are published to protect privacy.

nodes.label: Agent Configuration Section
nodes.rationale: Declares runtime, enabled skills, channels, proactive flag, and heartbeat_interval in the manifest so each node's agent behavior is configuration-driven and auditable rather than hardcoded.

nodes.label: Bootstrap Interviewer Skill
nodes.rationale: Replaces manual file creation with a guided ~10 minute interview so non-technical operators can bootstrap SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md, data registries, and federation.yaml; the same question set doubles as a web form for non-tech operators.

nodes.label: Approval-Required Mode (Draft → Present → Confirm → Execute)
nodes.author: organizational-os
nodes.rationale: The agent never executes transactions autonomously: every capital action passes draft → present → confirm → execute with the human operator executing, because financial operations are irreversible and high-impact; the default when in doubt is draft and present, never act.

nodes.label: Funding Scout Skill
nodes.author: organizational-os
nodes.rationale: Maintains a local registry (data/funding-opportunities.yaml) with deadline escalation into HEARTBEAT.md (30-day and 7-day alerts) and a minimum active pipeline of 5 opportunities; never submits applications autonomously — draft and present for operator approval.

nodes.label: Heartbeat Monitor Skill
nodes.author: organizational-os
nodes.rationale: HEARTBEAT.md is treated as the organizational nervous system: proactive monitoring categorizes tasks by urgency (critical/urgent/upcoming/ongoing) and deletes stale tasks ruthlessly because a bloated heartbeat is useless.

nodes.label: Idea Scout Skill
nodes.rationale: Scans the processed knowledge commons for gap language ('there is no...', 'missing...') and repeated themes, then evaluates novelty/relevance/feasibility/evidence/impact before surfacing, so ideas are evidence-backed and never duplicate existing projects.

nodes.label: Idea Lifecycle (surfaced → hatched)
nodes.rationale: Stages surfaced → proposed → approved → developing → hatched → archived map escalating human commitment (agent → community champion → council → developers → independent repo), keeping agent-detected ideas gated behind human review before resources are committed.

nodes.label: Knowledge Curator Skill
nodes.author: organizational-os
nodes.rationale: Curation principles: synthesize don't copy, source everything, domain-tag everything, distinguish signal from noise, apply org voice — turning ephemeral channel flow into durable, navigable knowledge; privacy boundary is 'open by default, private by exception' with ideas synthesized rather than individuals quoted.

nodes.label: Meeting Processor Skill
nodes.author: organizational-os
nodes.rationale: Transcripts are synthesized into structured notes (decisions, action items, summary) rather than stored verbatim; action items fan out to HEARTBEAT.md and project pages so meeting outcomes become operational state instead of dead text.

nodes.label: Org-OS Session Lifecycle Skill
nodes.rationale: OPEN → PLAN → EXECUTE → CLOSE workflow bookends every session with git sync so the operator never has to remember it; sync failures never block a session, and the close-time memory write is mandatory because it is the thread connecting sessions.

nodes.label: Research Skill
nodes.rationale: All research outputs land in docs/research/ with .provenance.md citation sidecars, and findings are deliberately fed back into ideas, funding, knowledge, tasks, and memory so research is never a dead-end artifact.

nodes.label: Feynman Research Framework
nodes.rationale: Dispatches specialized agents (researcher, reviewer, writer, verifier) to produce source-heavy artifacts with inline citations, chosen so research claims are verifiable via provenance tracking.

nodes.label: Schema Generator Skill
nodes.author: organizational-os
nodes.rationale: Regenerates EIP-4824 JSON-LD schemas in .well-known/ from data/*.yaml so machine-readable organizational identity stays current with actual operational data; dao.json is the entry point referencing all other schema URIs.

nodes.label: Workspace Improver Skill
nodes.rationale: Autonomous improvement is bounded: one scoped, reversible change per cycle with before/after metrics and keep-or-revert evaluation; identity files (SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md, federation.yaml, MASTERPLAN.md) must never be modified without a human.

nodes.label: Autoresearch Pattern
nodes.rationale: Maps the org workspace onto karpathy/autoresearch: MASTERPLAN.md = program.md (human directions), data/*.yaml + skills/ = train.py (editable surface), HEARTBEAT.md metrics = val_bpb (evaluation), memory logs = experiment log — so agents improve the workspace via measured experiments instead of unbounded edits.
